dedupe_keys.name: jakarta urban material solar radiation and surface temperature measurements

description: This Mendeley Data deposit contains field measurements of incoming and outgoing solar radiation and surface temperature for fifteen urban material types in Jakarta, Indonesia. Researchers observed each material at five-minute intervals for thirty to 120 minutes and recorded coordinates, land-use class, material type, albedo and measurement date. The current public version 2 consists of one CSV and states CC BY 4.0. It adds weather-context fields to the earlier release cited in the article. Coverage is a set of short urban-surface campaigns, not continuous citywide heat monitoring or directly measured human heat exposure. Material placement, changing weather and unequal observation windows matter when comparing reflective or thermal response. A reviewer-assessed use is checking material-level parameters or surface-temperature patterns in urban heat simulations. No related catalogue record was verified as using the same material measurements. The article’s version-1 DOI and release-2 URL differ; the current repository DOI is used here. No CSV values or microclimate model were downloaded. These conditions limit extrapolation to other urban materials or seasons. A limitation is the unequal, short observation window across materials.
